source_facts.fact: Defra's national standards were published 19 June 2025 and updated 30 July 2025; they contain seven standards covering runoff destinations, everyday rainfall, extreme rainfall/flooding, water quality, amenity, biodiversity and lifecycle/structural design.
source_facts.gate: National standards guide design and operation but do not constitute a parcel drainage approval or planning permission.

source_facts.fact: Flood-risk PPG gives a preferred surface-water discharge hierarchy: infiltration, surface-water body, surface-water sewer/highway drain/other drainage system, then combined sewer.
source_facts.gate: A preferred hierarchy is not evidence that the first option is technically feasible on a specific parcel.

source_facts.fact: PPG says that for major development with surface-water drainage the local planning authority must consult the lead local flood authority.
source_facts.gate: LLFA consultation or advice is not the local planning authority's final planning decision.

source_facts.fact: NPPF paragraph 182 says applications that could affect drainage on or around a site should incorporate proportionate SuDS, with major-development systems taking account of LLFA advice and maintenance arrangements.
source_facts.gate: Policy expectation is not a completed drainage design, adoption agreement or approval.

source_facts.fact: Approved Document H covers building-regulation requirements for drainage and waste disposal.
source_facts.gate: Building Regulations compliance is separate from planning permission and site-specific flood-risk acceptability.

source_facts.fact: LLFAs lead local surface-water, groundwater and ordinary-watercourse risk management and prepare strategic documents and investigations.
source_facts.gate: Strategic flood-management responsibility or a Section 19 investigation does not itself determine a development drainage solution.

official_measurement_examples.name: National SuDS standards publication state
official_measurement_examples.fact: Published 19 June 2025 and updated 30 July 2025; seven standards cover runoff, rainfall/flooding, water quality, amenity, biodiversity and lifecycle design.

official_measurement_examples.name: SuDS drainage hierarchy
official_measurement_examples.fact: PPG preference is infiltration, surface-water body, surface-water sewer/highway drain/other drainage system, then combined sewer.

official_measurement_examples.name: LLFA major-development consultation
official_measurement_examples.fact: For major development with surface-water drainage the LPA must consult the LLFA.

official_measurement_examples.name: NPPF paragraph 182 SuDS scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Applications affecting drainage should incorporate proportionate SuDS; major-development systems should take account of LLFA advice and maintenance arrangements.

official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document H scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document H covers Building Regulations for drainage and waste disposal in England.

official_measurement_examples.name: LLFA statutory role distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Croydon states the LLFA provides a substantive surface-water response while planning decision-making remains with the LPA.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surface Water Management Plan scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Defra's SWMP guidance is an overarching framework for local authorities to coordinate local surface-water flood-risk management.

official_measurement_examples.name: London Sustainable Drainage Action Plan scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: London's action plan promotes retrofitting and wider SuDS uptake to reduce pressure on drains and sewers.

core_rules: national SuDS standards are design standards not parcel planning permission
SuDS standard compliance must not be claimed without a site design and evidence
drainage hierarchy expresses preference and does not prove infiltration feasibility
infiltration suitability requires ground and groundwater evidence
surface-water-body discharge requires applicable consent and capacity checks
surface-water sewer availability does not prove connection approval
combined sewer is lower in the hierarchy and must not be assumed acceptable
LLFA consultation is advice to the LPA and not the final planning decision
LLFA non-objection is not a sewer adoption agreement
LLFA objection is not itself final planning refusal
major-development status must be determined from the actual proposal
SuDS policy for major development does not prove the submitted scheme is compliant
maintenance arrangements must not be assumed from planning-policy text
adoption responsibility must not be guessed from a SuDS feature type
water-company adoption criteria are distinct from planning approval
Building Regulations Part H is distinct from planning permission
building-control compliance does not determine flood-risk planning acceptability
foul drainage and surface-water drainage must remain distinct
surface-water drainage and groundwater flood risk must remain distinct
ordinary watercourse consent is distinct from SuDS planning approval
main-river permitting is distinct from LLFA drainage advice
Internal Drainage Board requirements must not be inferred outside an IDB district
SuDS features can provide biodiversity amenity and water-quality benefits but those benefits must not be fabricated
rainwater harvesting potential is not a guaranteed water-supply saving
interception performance must not be invented without design calculations
extreme-rainfall performance requires design event and climate allowance inputs
runoff-rate calculations require site area and hydrological inputs
greenfield runoff rate must not be fabricated from land-use label alone
brownfield drainage cannot automatically use historic discharge as acceptable baseline
infiltration tests cannot be inferred from soil map alone
groundwater Source Protection Zone can affect infiltration suitability but does not universally prohibit SuDS
contaminated-land context can constrain infiltration and requires site-specific assessment
surface-water flood-map risk is screening evidence not a drainage design
strategic flood-risk assessment is not a site drainage approval
surface-water management plan is strategic evidence not parcel permission
local flood-risk strategy is not a site-specific drainage condition
Section 19 flood investigation is historic/event evidence not a future drainage guarantee
FRMP measures are strategic and not proof of a local scheme's delivery
funded flood scheme is not completed infrastructure unless delivery is evidenced
drainage maintenance plan is not implemented maintenance without responsible-body evidence
SuDS approval does not prove planning conditions are discharged
planning permission does not prove SuDS construction or maintenance performance
retrofit SuDS strategy is not evidence that a parcel already contains SuDS
citywide drainage programme totals must not be downscaled to parcel capacity
NO_DATA must not be converted into no surface-water constraint
screening drainage evidence must remain separate from candidate promotion
no parcel drainage design connection approval planning outcome or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel drainage accuracy
